pairs.difference: A: the striped towel runs diagonally corner to corner and nearly touches the left edge (margin 0.037, width 0.923, just over the real range). B: the calculator is tilted and held well inside the card (margin 0.144, over the real range), with faint pi symbols behind it that stay quiet at thumbnail size. Both name themselves instantly. Each misses the range by a small amount, in opposite directions, so neither gives a reason to choose.

A: the oil lamp is a narrow column (width 0.426, under the real range), but the glass bulb and brass bowl give it mass, and the handle breaks the symmetry. B: the candelabra stands dead-centre and square-on, a perfectly mirrored object. Its thin stem and arms cover very little of the card (area 0.147, lowest in the set), so at thumbnail size it reads as three flames on a wiry line with violet showing through. Weak call, since both cards are thin.
pairs.fix: Draw the candelabra much larger and turned slightly to three-quarter view, with thick chunky arms and a heavy base, so the gold shape fills the card and one arm comes close to the edge.

pairs.difference: A: the pumpkin is a large round mass centered low, with even clearance all around (margin 0.133, over the real range) and nothing near an edge. B: the duck rider fills the height, and the beak and tail reach toward the sides (margin 0.098), though the pebbles add small side detail. The pumpkin reads first and clearly; the only signal is the safe, evenly inset placement, as on the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Push the pumpkin closer to the camera and slightly off-center, so its side nearly touches the card edge and the table takes less room.

pairs.difference: A: the fountain sits wide across the card (width 0.916, margin 0.035), and the paving runs off the edges, so the object feels planted in its setting. B: the cat is a narrow upright shape (width 0.635, just under the real range) placed whole on a plain floor with empty striped wall on both sides. The curled tail is the only thing reaching toward the right. It reads quickly, but it sits small and safe inside the frame, like the generated lesson cards.
pairs.fix: Draw the black cat bigger and closer, filling the card width, with the tail nearly reaching the right edge and the ears close to the top.

pairs.difference: A: the graduation cap is a wide, floating, tilted shape over concentric rings (height 0.506, just under the real range). B: the witch hat is a floating tilted shape on the same kind of rings, with the brim near the sides (height 0.671, margin 0.065). Both are single objects with no rival focus, and both read at once. Framing gives no reason to choose.

A: this is the real lighthouse from the lesson cards. It is cropped by the bottom edge, with a single hero and no rival. B: the crooked house is shown whole from roof tip to grass (height 0.917), and the bright yellow moon behind the chimney is the lightest, roundest shape on the card. At thumbnail size the moon fights the many lit windows and the purple roofs, so the first read is split.
pairs.fix: Remove the moon. Draw the house larger and cropped by the bottom edge, with the sky left calm so the glowing windows are the only bright spot.

pairs.difference: A: the cauldron is centered square-on and whole, with even clearance (margin 0.086), every part inside the card, and the bubbles and flame stacked neatly on the center line. B: the gloves are pushed hard to the right edge (width 0.951, margin 0.021), overlapping each other and off-balance, with a bare band of wood below. B's numbers are outside the range, but the lessons run the other way: real cards push the hero to the edge and generated ones center it safely.
pairs.fix: Turn the cauldron to three-quarter view and push it off-center and closer, so a handle nearly touches the card edge and the floor shows less.

pairs.difference: A: the lion statue is one of the real reference cards, and it sits on a plinth in a park scene (area 0.444). B: the yellow bag is large and fills the card (area 0.467, just over the range). The towel, bottle and lotion rising from the top stay below the bag in the hierarchy, and the house patch holds the center. The first read is clearly a bag. Nothing in B's framing sets it apart from A.

A: the red scarf is a compact, centered mass with its badge at the middle, in the real range for width and height. B: the broom runs thinly from top right to bottom left. Only the yellow bristles have weight, so most of the card is empty wavy blue (area 0.149, under the real range). At thumbnail size the handle almost disappears and the hero looks small for its span.
pairs.fix: Draw the broom with a much thicker handle and a bigger bristle head, closer to the camera, so the yellow head fills the lower half of the card.

pairs.difference: A: the coffin is large and tilted, but it is wrapped in extras: gray headstones at both edges, bushes and clouds, each adding a small rival shape around the hero. It also keeps a safe clearance (margin 0.086, just over the real range). B: the stone table is framed by trees and a path, but the scenery stays darker and softer, and the table is close to the side (margin 0.044). Added side props are the same habit as the generated lighthouse with its lifebuoy and bushes.
pairs.fix: Remove the headstones and bushes. Draw the coffin bigger and closer on plain grass under a calm sky, with one corner nearly reaching the card edge.

pairs.difference: A: the crystal ball sits dead-centre and symmetric on a stand, with wide even clearance (margin 0.148, well over the real range) and a flat band of shelf below. It is clear at once but static and inset. B: the drink is upright, and the straw and umbrella break out diagonally toward the top corners (height 0.89, margin 0.05), which uses the card more fully.
pairs.fix: Draw the crystal ball bigger, nearly touching the left and right edges, slightly off-center, and show less of the shelf.

pairs.difference: A: the sneakers sit low and wide (height 0.487, under the real range, margin 0.033), with an empty orange top third, though the pair reaches close to the side. B: the gravestone stands whole, with the widest clearance of the set (margin 0.162) and a narrow width (0.605) on a plain two-tone backdrop. The hero is held far from every edge, with bare space around it and tiny moss and leaf accents that vanish at thumbnail size.
pairs.fix: Draw the gravestone much bigger and closer, wide enough to nearly touch the card sides, with its base cropped close to the bottom edge.

pattern: Generated cards keep the whole object safely inset and centered, with even clearance on all sides. Margins often run above the real range (0.13 to 0.16 on p03, p11, p12), and the object is rarely cropped or pushed against an edge. Thin objects are left at their natural thinness, so the hero is small for its span (candelabra, broom). Generated cards also add side props that split the first read (the moon in p06, the headstones in p10). Real cards go tighter and take more risk: heroes reach the edge, get cropped, or sit off balance. These are tendencies only: framing separates the pairs weakly except p06, and p05, p01 and p08 gave no compositional reason to choose.
